rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology/Case Study <U+2013> authors run a coupled MIKE SHE/MIKE 11 model of the Mosuowan irrigation district with their own climate, soil, stream flow, irrigation and groundwater data, calibrated (Jan<U+2013>Aug 2006) and tested (Sep<U+2013>Dec 2006) against observed groundwater depths at 10 sites (Fig. 3, Table 2). Q2: Results 'Effect of Irrigation Methods on Groundwater Recharge Intensity', Fig. 4 and Conclusions <U+2013> simulated daily recharge under flood irrigation (peaks 0.57 and 0.47 mm/d) versus water-saving irrigation (max 0.42, min 0.1 mm/d); authors conclude water-saving irrigation weakens recharge intensity and lowers groundwater level (Fig. 6, difference 0.37 m); intro equates water-saving irrigation with drip irrigation; model output compared with measured groundwater depths (E = 0.84, R = 0.92<U+2013>0.98). Q6: Case Study description <U+2013> results reported for the whole Mosuowan irrigation district (about 45,100 ha), with spatial mapping of recharge-intensity change (Fig. 5: 10.22% decreasing, 1.41% increasing, 88.37% no change).
rows.notes: Study refers to 'water-saving irrigation' throughout but explicitly identifies it with drip irrigation in the introduction (cotton district in Xinjiang), so technology taken as matching, with some residual doubt. Q2 caveat: model validated only against 2006 observations; the flood-irrigation period (1991<U+2013>1992) is simulated with the same model but no comparison against 1991<U+2013>1992 observations is shown. Q3 no: single modelling method; observed groundwater depths serve only for calibration/validation, not as an independent estimate of recharge. Q4 no: recharge flux is the claimed effect itself; the study does not separately report return flow/deep percolation or the irrigation water balance as an intermediate variable, and the explanation given (larger irrigated area with unchanged total supply, land-use change) is asserted rather than quantified. Q5 no: one district, one main crop (cotton). Q7 no: no condition stated as a requirement; only explanatory reasons. Q8 no: no limitations of own result stated (general caveats on numerical models are cited from other work). Q9 no: only validation metrics (E, R, RMSE, 5<U+2013>95% regression bounds) and monthly max/min recharge values; no dispersion or propagated uncertainty on the recharge difference.
